title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools (People Ops Handbook)
author: Ava Thompson
summary: Comprehensive People Ops handbook entry covering role families and ladders, benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding flow, and the core internal tools and access patterns used at Redwood Inference.
body:
Purpose:

This page is the canonical company handbook entry maintained by People Ops for new and existing employees at Redwood Inference. It summarizes role families and career ladders, the benefits and perks we offer, the hiring and onboarding flow, and the core internal tools and access patterns. Use this as a reference and follow links to team-specific pages for detailed procedures.

1) Working at Redwood — core principles:

- Developer-first culture: decisions prioritize engineer productivity, clear SLOs for customer-facing systems, and measurable outcomes.
- Ownership and clarity: job descriptions focus on end-to-end ownership, measurable deliverables, and cross-team collaboration.
- Growth mindset: career ladders emphasize coaching, measurable impact, and clear promotion criteria.
- Psychological safety and inclusion: we run structured 1:1s, inclusive hiring, and anti-bias training for interviewers.

2) Roles and career ladders (overview):

Redwood maintains role families for Engineering, Product, Research (Applied ML), SRE/Infra, Design, and Go-to-Market. Each family has levels with clear expectations. Below is a summary of the engineering ladder as an example; team pages contain full rubrics.

Engineering career ladder (summary):

- E1 / Associate Engineer: Contributes to well-scoped tasks, writes tests and documentation, asks clarifying questions.
- E2 / Software Engineer: Delivers features with minimal guidance, owns small services, participates in design reviews.
- E3 / Senior Software Engineer: Leads designs for cross-service features, mentors others, defines metrics and SLOs.
- E4 / Staff Engineer: Defines architecture across multiple teams, drives technical strategy, leads large cross-team initiatives.
- E5 / Principal / Senior Staff: Sets company-level technical direction, influences product strategy, and leads hiring and technical roadmaps.

Promotion and calibration process (high level):

1. Candidate drafts promotion packet (impact examples, PRs, metrics, mentorship).
2. Manager collects calibration feedback and writes an assessment.
3. Promotion committee review (peer reviewers + hiring manager).
4. Outcome shared with candidate and HR updates compensation/level.

Expectations for promotion: sustained impact (typically 3-9 months of demonstrable outcomes), competency across technical and behavioral dimensions, and alignment with the published rubric. Team-specific rubrics provide measurable examples.

3) Benefits and perks (high-level summary):

Core benefits (US & EU parity where applicable):

- Health: medical, dental, and vision plans (employer-subsidized tiers).
- Time off: 20 days PTO baseline in addition to public holidays, flexible parental leave policy (16 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary, local adjustments).
- Retirement: 401(k) with employer matching (US) and country-appropriate equivalents.
- Flexible working: hybrid policy with recommended in-office days per team; full remote options available for approved roles.
- Equity: full-time employees receive equity grants with standard 4-year vesting and one-year cliff.
- Learning & development: $1,500 annual learning stipend and quarterly peer-led technical guilds.
- Wellness: monthly wellness stipend and access to mental health resources and EAP.

Perks and operational support:

- Hardware allowance: new hires receive an initial allowance for laptop and peripherals; refresh policy every 36 months.
- Home office stipend for remote/home setup.
- Commuter and dependent-care benefits where applicable.
- Team offsites budget and celebration allowances.

How to enroll or make changes:

1. Benefits portal: log into the People Ops portal (link available from Confluence homepage).
2. Open enrollment: annual window communicated via Slack and email.
3. Exceptions: submit a benefits exception request ticket to people-ops@redwood.com.

4) Hiring and onboarding overview:

Hiring principles:

- Hire for potential and culture-add: we value curiosity, ownership, and technical depth.
- Structured interviewing: every role uses a standard interview plan and scorecards.
- Inclusive hiring: interviewers complete anti-bias training; candidate accommodations are supported.

Hiring workflow (simplified):

1. Requisition creation: hiring manager opens a req in the ATS and confirms approvals (finance + people-ops).
2. Sourcing & screening: recruiting sources candidates, and the recruiter performs a phone screen.
3. Technical loop: role-specific interviews (coding, design, system design, behavioral).
4. Debrief and scorecard: interviewers submit scorecards within 48 hours.
5. Offer: people-ops generates the offer, manager calibrates compensation band, and the recruiter extends the offer.

Offer & negotiation guidance:

- Compensation bands: published internally; managers consult people-ops for exceptions.
- Standard offer components: base salary, equity grant summary, benefits summary, and start date.
- Negotiations: escalated to hiring manager + people-ops for review.

Onboarding timeline (first 90 days):

Week 0 (pre-start):
- Complete paperwork in HR portal, choose benefits, and confirm hardware preference.
- Receive welcome message and onboarding schedule.

Week 1:
- Orientation: company mission, org overview, security training, and intro to core tools.
- Manager 1:1 to review role, goals, and first projects.
- Setup: laptop, Slack, GitHub access, Google Workspace, and Confluence.

Weeks 2-4:
- Deep dives with partner teams, onboarding project assigned, weekly 1:1s.
- Complete mandatory compliance and security training.

Months 2-3:
- Deliver first project milestone, participate in team planning, and get feedback checkpoints at 30 and 90 days.
- Career conversation: expectations for the next 6-12 months and a growth plan.

Manager checklist (essential items):

- Send welcome note and first-week schedule before start.
- Assign a buddy and onboarding project.
- Create 30/60/90 goals with measurable outcomes.
- Ensure access and clear tasks for the first two sprints.

5) Internal tools guide (core systems and access patterns):

This section lists primary internal tools, owners, and access notes. For team-level tooling refer to the team wiki pages.

Key systems:

- Identity & Access:
  - Okta (SSO) — owner: Security. Use Okta for single sign-on to Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub, and the internal apps portal.
  - Access requests: use the Access Portal (link in Okta) to request additional permissions; approvals route to service owners.

- Code & CI:
  - GitHub Enterprise — owner: eng-developer-experience. Branch protection rules are enforced; use PR templates.
  - CI/CD: Buildkite pipelines — owner: eng-infra. Tests must pass on main and release branches.

- Issue tracking & planning:
  - Jira — owner: eng-platform. Tickets follow standard templates for incidents, features, and bugs.
  - Roadmaps: Product uses the Roadmaps board; engineering links epics to delivery milestones.

- Documentation & knowledge base:
  - Confluence — owner: eng-developer-experience. This page is part of the company-handbook space. Use templates for runbooks, ADRs, and design docs.

- Observability & incident tools:
  - Datadog — owner: eng-sre. Dashboards for service SLOs, error rates, and latency.
  - PagerDuty — owner: eng-sre. On-call schedules and escalation policies are managed here.

- People systems:
  - HR/Payroll portal (Workday / Gusto) — owner: people-ops. Benefits enrollment, payroll information, and time off.
  - Learning platform (LMS) — owner: people-ops. Enroll for courses and record completed training.

Access and onboarding to tools:

- Default access: new employees receive baseline access to Slack, Google Workspace, Confluence, GitHub (read), and the HR portal.
- Sensitive access: production systems, billing consoles, and KMS require role-based approvals; follow the Access Request procedure and get manager + service owner approvals.
- Secrets and keys: use HashiCorp Vault (or company secret manager) for credential storage. Never check secrets into repos.

Sample access request table:

| System | Default access | Request path | Approver |
| Okta | SSO account | Auto-provision | Security team |
| GitHub | Read access to org | Manager request via Access Portal | Eng DevX owner |
| Production cluster | No default access | Access Portal + infra review | Eng Infra owner |

6) Policies & escalation contact points:

- Code of conduct: mandatory for all employees; violations reported to people-ops and legal.
- Security incidents: report to security@redwood.com and follow the incident runbook in security-and-compliance.
- HR escalations: people-ops@redwood.com or anonymous reporting via the Whistleblower form.

7) Contacts, ownership, and where to go next:

- Document owner: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.com).
- Onboarding coordinator: Mariah Lopez (mariah.lopez@redwood.com).
- Benefits questions: benefits@redwood.com.
- Technical access & GitHub issues: eng-devex@redwood.com.

Related pages and templates:

- New hire checklist (use for each new employee): /confluence/company-handbook/new-hire-checklist-2026.json
- Engineering ladder rubric: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/engineering-ladder-rubric-2025.json

Appendix: quick CLI snippets and examples:

- Requesting access via Access Portal: open Okta > Company Apps > Access Portal > Submit request and attach justification.
- Typical onboarding PR template: see Confluence templates for code contribution and design doc templates.
